review_output: {"summary":"Not ready to merge. Deleting a Live or Vendor that has metric data, or changing a submission's live, probably fails now. That is a regression in existing product flows. Some lifetime checks can be bypassed because the database trusts timestamps the caller supplies. Session invariants are only partly enforced and can race. The per-interval revision counter puts every write for a version on one row, and the report claim locks rows in the wrong order. The 43 tests never delete a Live/Vendor, backdate a timestamp, overlap intervals or race a close.","findings":[{"issue":"Deleting a Live/Vendor and moving a submission to another live can be blocked by the metric foreign keys","severity":"BLOCKER","area":"lifecycle/regression","file":"migration (LiveMetricRegistration FKs + wp20_metric_scope_update)","evidence":"LiveMetricRegistration(liveId,submissionId) references FormSubmission(liveId,id) with ON UPDATE CASCADE. FormSubmission.liveId is ON DELETE SET NULL from Live. So deleting a Live (or a Vendor, which cascades to it) nulls the submission key and cascades liveId=NULL into the Registration row. That fails twice: the column is NOT NULL, and the scope-immutable trigger raises 23514. Changing FormSubmission.liveId directly fails the same way. Separately, the Registration.visitorId FK is ON DELETE RESTRICT. Because RESTRICT is checked immediately, deleting a version (which cascades to both visitors and registrations) can fail depending on the order the cascades run. No test deletes a Live, Vendor or version.","impact":"Existing delete-live, delete-vendor (account deletion) and submission-reassignment flows fail once any metric registration exists.","recommended_fix":"Point the submission FK at FormSubmission(id) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE NO ACTION, and validate liveId/vendor in the guard trigger. Change visitorId to ON DELETE NO ACTION (or CASCADE). Change scope FKs to ON UPDATE NO ACTION / RESTRICT so they cannot fight the immutability triggers.","required_test":"With the full a/b fixture: delete Live a, delete Vendor a, delete version a, and update a submission's liveId. Each should either succeed with the metric rows cleaned up or fail on purpose. Tenant b's rows must stay unchanged.","confidence":0.75},{"issue":"Lifetime checks trust receivedAt and createdAt values that the caller supplies","severity":"MAJOR","area":"invariants/lifecycle","file":"migration (wp20_metric_interval_guard, wp20_metric_session_guard, LiveMetricInterval_values_check)","evidence":"Expiry checks compare against NEW.\"receivedAt\": version, session and admission expiry, plus receivedAt >= wallEndAt. The session guard compares a.\"expiresAt\" > NEW.\"createdAt\". Both columns are writable defaults, not server clock values. Backdating receivedAt lets an interval through on an expired admission or version. The tests only cover receivedAt values that would be rejected.","impact":"The database does not enforce the 'expired admission cannot supply evidence' and 'future exposure' rules it claims to enforce, so evidence after expiry can be stored.","recommended_fix":"In BEFORE INSERT, force NEW.receivedAt := statement_timestamp() (and NEW.createdAt likewise), or compare against statement_timestamp() and reject caller-supplied values.","required_test":"Expire the admission, then insert an interval with receivedAt backdated before the expiry; it must be rejected. Do the same for a session whose createdAt is backdated.","confidence":0.8},{"issue":"Session order, overlap and completion rules are not enforced, and inserts can race a session close","severity":"MAJOR","area":"concurrency/invariants","file":"migration (wp20_metric_interval_guard, wp20_metric_session_guard)","evidence":"The interval guard never compares sequence with lastSequence, never advances lastSequence/lastElapsedMs, and never checks that wall or media ranges are continuous with the previous interval. Gaps, out-of-order inserts and overlapping intervals (for example sequences 2 and 3 with the same wall range) are all accepted. complete=true only requires closedAt, not a final contiguous sequence, which contradicts the schema doc. The guard reads the session, submission and admission without FOR SHARE/UPDATE. An interval insert can therefore commit after a concurrent close, verification revocation or admission release.","impact":"Watch time can be double-counted. 'Complete' sessions may have gaps. Evidence can be appended after a session is closed or revoked.","recommended_fix":"In the interval trigger, lock the session row FOR UPDATE and require sequence = lastSequence+1 and wallStartAt >= the previous wallEndAt. Then advance lastSequence/lastElapsedMs in the same transaction. Lock the admission and submission rows FOR SHARE. Allow complete=true only when lastSequence matches a recorded final sequence.","required_test":"Insert a sequence gap, an overlapping wall range, and a duplicate range under a new sequence; all must be rejected. Race a session close against an interval insert, and a verification revocation against an insert; no interval may be stored after the close or revocation.","confidence":0.75},{"issue":"Every evidence write updates the same version row, and the report trigger locks rows in an order that can deadlock","severity":"MAJOR","area":"concurrency","file":"migration (wp20_metric_evidence_changed, wp20_metric_report_invalidate, wp20_metric_report_guard)","evidence":"Every visitor, registration, session or interval write runs UPDATE LiveMetricVersion SET sourceRevision+1, so all viewers of a version wait on one row lock until commit. That update then updates report rows. A worker's UPDATE on a report locks the report row first; its BEFORE trigger then takes SELECT version FOR SHARE. One transaction holds version → report and the other holds report → version, so they can deadlock. The comment says workers lock the version first, but the tested claim UPDATE does not.","impact":"Ingestion for a busy live is effectively processed one write at a time, the version table accumulates dead row versions, and report claims can deadlock (40P01) against ingestion.","recommended_fix":"Bump the revision once per statement (statement-level trigger), or keep it in a separate counter/event table. Have the report guard lock the version before the report row: claim through a function that does SELECT version FOR SHARE first. Alternatively, compare revisions with no lock and re-check at finalize.","required_test":"Run concurrent interval inserts across many sessions while workers claim and finalize reports in parallel. Expect no 40P01 deadlock and a bounded lock wait, and every finalized report should match the current sourceRevision.","confidence":0.65},{"issue":"Changing the Live's video or deleting the video does not invalidate an existing metric version","severity":"MINOR","area":"tenant isolation/invariants","file":"migration (wp20_metric_version_update)","evidence":"The source check (videoId matches the Live, same vendor) runs only on INSERT. LiveMetricVersion.videoId has no FK, and durationMs is not compared with Video.durationSec. Changing Live.videoId, or Video deletion (which sets Live.videoId to NULL), leaves the version collecting against stale content. sourceRevision also accepts any value the caller supplies at INSERT.","impact":"Metrics can keep being collected and reported for content the Live no longer plays, and durationMs bounds can be wrong.","recommended_fix":"Add a composite FK (vendorId, videoId) → Video(vendorId, id). Turn collection off, or reject intervals, when Live.videoId no longer matches. Force sourceRevision := 0 on INSERT.","required_test":"Change Live.videoId, or delete the video, then insert an interval; it must be rejected. Insert a version with sourceRevision=5; the stored value must be 0.","confidence":0.6}]}
